title: Quadratic Equations: The Formula and Completing the Square

short_title: Quadratic formula and completing the square
standard_text: solving quadratic equations in one variable by use of formula and by completing the square for y = x² + px + q
meta_desc: Free Secondary 3 maths worksheets on solving quadratic equations with the quadratic formula and by completing the square, with answers correct to 2 decimal places. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac)) ÷ 2a works for every quadratic equation.
key_sub: Make one side 0 first. To complete the square, add (half the coefficient of x)².
body_html:
How it works

For ax2 + bx + c = 0, the quadratic formula is x = (−b ± √(b2 − 4ac)) ÷ 2a. It works when the quadratic does not factorise.

To complete the square for x2 + px, add (p/2)2: x2 + 6x + 9 = (x + 3)2.

Make one side 0 first. Give answers correct to 2 decimal places unless the question says otherwise.

Example

Solve x2 − 4x − 1 = 0, correct to 2 decimal places.

a = 1, b = −4, c = −1, so b2 − 4ac = 20

x = (4 ± √20) ÷ 2

Answer: x = −0.24 or x = 4.24

Example

Solve x2 + 6x − 2 = 0 by completing the square.

x2 + 6x = 2

Add 9: (x + 3)2 = 11

x + 3 = ±√11

Answer: x = −6.32 or x = 0.32

Common mistakes

  • Using b instead of −b at the start of the formula.
  • Dividing only the square root by 2a. The whole top is divided.
  • Getting the sign of c wrong: for c = −3, −4ac is positive.
  • Adding p/2 instead of (p/2)2 when completing the square.

faq.q: When should I use the quadratic formula?
faq.a: Use it when the quadratic does not factorise easily, or when the question asks for answers correct to 2 decimal places or 3 significant figures.
Writing x² + px + q as (x + p/2)² − (p/2)² + q. Then you can solve by taking square roots of both sides.

faq.q: Why do I get two answers?
faq.a: Because a number and its negative have the same square, so ± gives two values of x. In a word problem, reject any answer that does not make sense, such as a negative length.
Then the equation has no real solutions, and the graph does not cut the x-axis.

Write x2 + 16x + 3 in the form (x + p)2 + q.
items.e: Half of 16 is 8. (x + 8)2 = x2 + 16x + 64, so subtract 64 to balance: 3 − 64 = −61. (x + 8)2 − 61.

items.q: What number should be added to x2 + 16x to make a perfect square?
items.e: Take half of 16 and square it: (8)2 = 64. Then x2 + 16x + 64 = (x + 8)2.

items.q: Write x2 − 14x + 9 in the form (x + p)2 + q.
items.e: Half of −14 is −7. (x − 7)2 = x2 − 14x + 49, so subtract 49 to balance: 9 − 49 = −40. (x − 7)2 − 40.

items.q: Solve x2 + 6x − 7 = 0 by completing the square.
items.e: Move −7: x2 + 6x = 7. Add 9 to both sides: (x + 3)2 = 16. Square root: x + 3 = ±4, so x = −7 or x = 1.

items.q: Write x2 − 14x − 9 in the form (x + p)2 + q.
items.e: Half of −14 is −7. (x − 7)2 = x2 − 14x + 49, so subtract 49 to balance: −9 − 49 = −58. (x − 7)2 − 58.

items.q: Write x2 − 2x − 5 in the form (x + p)2 + q.
items.e: Half of −2 is −1. (x − 1)2 = x2 − 2x + 1, so subtract 1 to balance: −5 − 1 = −6. (x − 1)2 − 6.

items.q: Write x2 − 14x + 5 in the form (x + p)2 + q.
items.e: Half of −14 is −7. (x − 7)2 = x2 − 14x + 49, so subtract 49 to balance: 5 − 49 = −44. (x − 7)2 − 44.

items.q: What number should be added to x2 − 6x to make a perfect square?
items.e: Take half of −6 and square it: (−3)2 = 9. Then x2 − 6x + 9 = (x − 3)2.

items.q: What number should be added to x2 + 6x to make a perfect square?
items.e: Take half of 6 and square it: (3)2 = 9. Then x2 + 6x + 9 = (x + 3)2.

items.q: Solve x2 − 6x + 5 = 0 by completing the square.
items.e: Move 5: x2 − 6x = −5. Add 9 to both sides: (x − 3)2 = 4. Square root: x − 3 = ±2, so x = 1 or x = 5.

items.q: Solve x2 + 4x − 45 = 0 by completing the square.
items.e: Move −45: x2 + 4x = 45. Add 4 to both sides: (x + 2)2 = 49. Square root: x + 2 = ±7, so x = −9 or x = 5.

items.q: Write x2 + 2x + 9 in the form (x + p)2 + q.
items.e: Half of 2 is 1. (x + 1)2 = x2 + 2x + 1, so subtract 1 to balance: 9 − 1 = 8. (x + 1)2 + 8.

items.q: Write x2 + 14x + 1 in the form (x + p)2 + q.
items.e: Half of 14 is 7. (x + 7)2 = x2 + 14x + 49, so subtract 49 to balance: 1 − 49 = −48. (x + 7)2 − 48.

items.q: Solve x2 − 16x + 28 = 0 by completing the square.
items.e: Move 28: x2 − 16x = −28. Add 64 to both sides: (x − 8)2 = 36. Square root: x − 8 = ±6, so x = 2 or x = 14.

items.q: What number should be added to x2 + 8x to make a perfect square?

items.q: Write x2 − 8x − 3 in the form (x + p)2 + q.
items.e: Half of −8 is −4. (x − 4)2 = x2 − 8x + 16, so subtract 16 to balance: −3 − 16 = −19. (x − 4)2 − 19.

items.q: Solve x2 − 8x − 33 = 0 by completing the square.
items.e: Move −33: x2 − 8x = 33. Add 16 to both sides: (x − 4)2 = 49. Square root: x − 4 = ±7, so x = −3 or x = 11.

items.q: Solve x2 + 8x + 7 = 0 by completing the square.
items.e: Move 7: x2 + 8x = −7. Add 16 to both sides: (x + 4)2 = 9. Square root: x + 4 = ±3, so x = −7 or x = −1.

items.q: Write x2 + 10x + 6 in the form (x + p)2 + q.

items.q: What number should be added to x2 + 12x to make a perfect square?
items.e: Take half of 12 and square it: (6)2 = 36. Then x2 + 12x + 36 = (x + 6)2.
